drivingQuestion: Is it obvious to Rabbi Yehuda that only the sciatic nerve of the right thigh is forbidden (דעת תורה), or is he uncertain which of the two thighs is forbidden (דעת נוטה)?
outcomeNote: The dilemma is settled: the baraita of two nerves from two thighs of two animals yields שמע מינה מיפשט פשיטא ליה, and Rava then supplies the source ״הירך״ – המיומנת שבירך. Everything from chullin.91a.19 onward is aggadic exposition rather than a dialectical resolution.

segments.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מִיפְשָׁט פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וּמַאי דַּעַת? דַּעַת תּוֹרָה, אוֹ דִלְמָא סַפּוֹקֵי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ, וּמַאי דַּעַת? דַּעַת נוֹטָה.
segments.en: «A dilemma was raised before» the Sages: Is it «obvious to Rabbi Yehuda» that the prohibition applies only to the sciatic nerve in the right thigh, «and» accordingly, «what» does he mean when he says that «logic» dictates? He means «the logic of the Torah. Or perhaps he is uncertain» as to whether it applies only to the right thigh or only to the left, «and» accordingly, «what» does he mean when he says that «logic» dictates? He means that «logic inclines» one to believe that the prohibition applies to the right thigh.

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָעֲצָמוֹת וְהַגִּידִים וְהַנּוֹתָר יִשָּׂרְפוּ לְשִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר. וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: הָנֵי גִּידֵי מַאי עֲבִידְתַּיְיהוּ? אִי גִּידֵי בָשָׂר – לֵיכְלִינְהוּ, וְאִי דְּאִיַּיתּוּר – הַיְינוּ נוֹתָר! אֶלָּא גִּידֵי צַוָּאר, אִי לָאו בָּשָׂר נִינְהוּ – לִישְׁדִּינְהוּ?
segments.en: The Gemara suggests: «Come» and «hear» a resolution based upon the following mishna (Pesaḥim 83a): «The bones» of the Paschal offering that contain edible marrow but cannot be eaten because it is prohibited to break the bones of the Paschal offering; «and the sinews; and the leftover» meat «should» all «be burned on the sixteenth» of Nisan, not on the fifteenth, the first day of Passover. «And we discussed it: What are the circumstances» in which «these sinews» must be burned? «If we say» they are «sinews of meat, let one eat them.» Why are they burned? «And if» they are sinews «that were left over» and not eaten, «that is» the case of «leftover» meat; why does the mishna list sinews separately? «Rather,» the mishna is referring to «sinews of the neck,» which are different from other sinews and are therefore mentioned separately. But «if they are not meat,» why do they require burning? «Let one» simply «discard them» like other waste.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְגִיד הַנָּשֶׁה, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר: אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בְּאַחַת.
segments.en: «And Rav Ḥisda said:» The mishna’s mention of sinews «is necessary only» in order to teach the halakha «of the sciatic nerve,» and «in accordance with» the opinion «of Rabbi Yehuda, who said:» The prohibition of the sciatic nerve «applies only to» the sciatic nerve in «one» of the animal’s thighs, and not to both.

segments.he: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא סַפּוֹקֵי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ – שַׁפִּיר, אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ מִיפְשָׁט פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ דְּהֶיתֵּירָא – לֵיכְלֵיהּ, דְּאִיסּוּרָא – לִשְׁדְּיֵיהּ!
segments.en: The Gemara explains how this resolves the dilemma: «Granted if you say» that Rabbi Yehuda «is uncertain» as to whether it is the sciatic nerve of the right or the left thigh, it works out «well.» Since it is uncertain which thigh may be eaten, one may not eat either of them, and one must burn each of them on the sixteenth due to the possibility that it was the permitted one and now has the status of leftover meat. «But if you say» that it is «obvious to» Rabbi Yehuda that the sciatic nerve of only the right thigh is forbidden, «let him eat» the sciatic nerve «of the permitted» left thigh, and «let him throw» away only the sciatic nerve «of the forbidden» right thigh. Neither one should be burned.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בַּר חֲנִינָא: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ מִיפְשָׁט פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן – כְּשֶׁהוּכְּרוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף נִתְעָרְבוּ.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «Rav Ika bar Ḥanina said: Actually I» could «say to you» that it is «obvious to» Rabbi Yehuda that the sciatic nerve of only the right thigh is forbidden. Nevertheless, «here we are dealing with» a case «where» the sciatic nerves «were identified» and removed, «but ultimately» the sciatic nerves «became intermingled» and one cannot tell which is from the right thigh and which is from the left thigh. Consequently, they must both be left over until the next day and then burned.

segments.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְשׇׁמְנוֹ, דְּתַנְיָא: שׇׁמְנוֹ מוּתָּר, וְיִשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים נָהֲגוּ בּוֹ אִיסּוּר.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi said:» The mishna’s ruling that the sinews must be burned «is necessary only» with regard to the «fat» around the sciatic nerve, «as it is taught» in a baraita: The «fat» around the sciatic nerve «is permitted» by Torah law, «but the Jewish people are holy» and «treated it as forbidden.» Since it is permitted by Torah law, it has the status of sacrificial meat and may not be simply discarded. Nevertheless, since the Jewish people treat it as forbidden, they do not eat it even from the Paschal offering, despite the mitzva to eat that offering in its entirety. Therefore, it is left until after the time when the meat may be eaten and it is burned as leftover sacrificial meat.

segments.he: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לְכִדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, שְׁנֵי גִידִין הֵן: פְּנִימִי סָמוּךְ לְעֶצֶם – אָסוּר, וְחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו; חִיצוֹן סָמוּךְ לְבָשָׂר – אָסוּר, וְאֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו.
segments.en: «Ravina said:» The mishna’s statement «is necessary only» with regard to the outer nerve, and it is «in accordance with that which Rav Yehuda» said that «Shmuel said. As Rav Yehuda said» that «Shmuel said: There are two nerves» included in the prohibition of the sciatic nerve. The «inner» nerve that is «next to the bone is forbidden» by Torah law, «and one is liable» to be flogged «for» eating «it.» The «outer» nerve that is «next to the flesh is forbidden» by rabbinic law, «and» therefore «one is not liable» to be flogged «for» eating «it.» In the case of a Paschal offering, since the outer nerve is permitted by Torah law, it assumes the status of leftover sacrificial meat when it is not eaten.

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָכַל מִזֶּה כְּזַיִת וּמִזֶּה כְּזַיִת – סוֹפֵג שְׁמוֹנִים, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ סוֹפֵג אֶלָּא אַרְבָּעִים.
segments.en: The Gemara suggests: «Come» and «hear» another resolution to the dilemma about Rabbi Yehuda’s statement, from a mishna (96a): If «one ate an olive-bulk from this» sciatic nerve of the right leg «and an olive-bulk from that» sciatic nerve of the left leg, «he incurs eighty» lashes. «Rabbi Yehuda says: He incurs only forty» lashes.

segments.he: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא מִיפְשָׁט פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ – שַׁפִּיר, אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ סַפּוֹקֵי מְסַפְּקָא לֵיהּ – הָוְיָא לַהּ הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק, וְשָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאָמַר: הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק לֹא שְׁמָהּ הַתְרָאָה.
segments.en: «Granted, if you say» it is «obvious to» Rabbi Yehuda that the sciatic nerve of the right thigh is the one forbidden by Torah law, it is «well. But if you say he is uncertain,» why would he hold that one incurs any lashes? When the individual is forewarned not to partake of each sciatic nerve, which is necessary in order to be liable for incurring lashes, «it is an uncertain forewarning, and we have heard» about «Rabbi Yehuda that he said: An uncertain forewarning is not characterized as forewarning.»

segments.he: דְּתַנְיָא: הִכָּה אֶת זֶה, וְחָזַר וְהִכָּה אֶת זֶה, קִלֵּל אֶת זֶה, וְחָזַר וְקִלֵּל אֶת זֶה, הִכָּה שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּבַת אַחַת, אוֹ שֶׁקִּלֵּל שְׁנֵיהֶם בְּבַת אַחַת – חַיָּיב. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בְּבַת אַחַת – חַיָּיב, בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה – פָּטוּר.
segments.en: «As it is taught» in a baraita: If one is uncertain which of two men is his father and he «struck this» one «and then struck that» one, or «cursed this» one «and then cursed that» one, or «struck both of them simultaneously, or cursed both of them simultaneously, he is liable» to receive the death penalty, as he certainly struck or cursed his father. «Rabbi Yehuda says:» If he struck or cursed both of them «simultaneously he is liable,» provided he was forewarned that his action will certainly render him liable to receive the death penalty. But if he struck or cursed them «one after the other he is exempt.» Apparently, Rabbi Yehuda is of the opinion that one is not punished after uncertain forewarning; since in this case it is impossible to determine which of them is the father, inevitably each forewarning is uncertain. Similarly, if Rabbi Yehuda is uncertain which sciatic nerve is forbidden by Torah law, he should hold that since the forewarning before eating either sciatic nerve is uncertain, one who consumes both should be exempt.

segments.he: הַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּאִידַּךְ תַּנָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר: הַתְרָאַת סָפֵק שְׁמָהּ הַתְרָאָה.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «This tanna» of that mishna, on 96a, «holds in accordance with» the opinion of «another tanna» with regard to the opinion «of Rabbi Yehuda, who said» that Rabbi Yehuda holds that «an uncertain forewarning is characterized as forewarning.»

segments.he: דְּתַנְיָא: ״לֹא תוֹתִירוּ מִמֶּנּוּ עַד בֹּקֶר וְגוֹ׳״ – בָּא הַכָּתוּב לִיתֵּן עֲשֵׂה אַחַר לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה, לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
segments.en: «As it is taught» in a baraita: The verse states with regard to the Paschal offering: «“And you shall not leave any of it until morning;» but that which remains of it until morning you shall burn with fire” (Exodus 12:10). «The verse comes to provide a positive mitzva» to burn the leftover meat «after» it has taught «a prohibition» against leaving it over, «to say that one is not flogged for» violation «of» the prohibition; this is «the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.» Rabbi Yehuda holds that one is not flogged for any transgression that can be rectified by the performance of a positive mitzva.

segments.he: רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִן הַשֵּׁם הוּא זֶה, אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה, וְכׇל לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה – אֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו.
segments.en: «Rabbi Ya’akov says: This,» the halakha that one is not flogged, «is not for» that «reason. Rather,» it is «because» leaving over sacrificial meat «is a prohibition that does not involve an action,» as one violates the prohibition through failure to take action, «and» concerning «any prohibition that does not involve an action, one is not flogged for» its violation. The forewarning one could receive for this transgression is an uncertain one, because witnesses who forewarn the individual cannot be certain until daybreak that he will leave it over. Nevertheless, this baraita indicates that if not for the fact that leaving over sacrificial meat can be rectified by a positive mitzva, Rabbi Yehuda would hold that one is flogged for leaving over sacrificial meat.

segments.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: אָכַל שְׁנֵי גִידִין מִשְּׁתֵּי יְרֵכוֹת מִשְּׁתֵּי בְהֵמוֹת – סוֹפֵג שְׁמוֹנִים; רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ סוֹפֵג אֶלָּא אַרְבָּעִים.
segments.en: The Gemara suggests: «Come» and «hear» a resolution of the uncertainty with regard to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda from a baraita: If «one ate two» sciatic «nerves from two thighs of two» different «animals, he incurs eighty» lashes. «Rabbi Yehuda says: He incurs only forty» lashes.

segments.he: מִדְּקָאָמַר מִשְׁתֵּי יְרֵכוֹת מִשְּׁתֵּי בְהֵמוֹת, פְּשִׁיטָא דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ לְאִיסּוּרָא, וּלְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אִיצְטְרִיךְ. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִיפְשָׁט פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara comments: «From» the fact that the first tanna «said» that he was referring to «two thighs of two» different «animals,» it is «obvious» that he meant they were both from the right thigh, because if one were from the right thigh and one were from the left thigh it would not matter if they were from two different animals or from the same animal. Consequently, «both» sciatic nerves are definitely «forbidden» by Torah law, and according to the first tanna one incurs eighty lashes for eating them. «And» it «was necessary» to teach that «according to Rabbi Yehuda» one incurs only forty lashes, as will be explained. «Conclude from» this baraita that it is «obvious to» Rabbi Yehuda that it is the sciatic nerve of the right thigh that is forbidden by Torah law. The Gemara affirms: «Conclude from» it that this is Rabbi Yehuda’s opinion.

segments.he: וְאִי פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ, אַמַּאי סוֹפֵג אַרְבָּעִים וְתוּ לָא? לִילְקֵי שְׁמוֹנִים! הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן – כְּגוֹן דְּלֵית בּוֹ כְּזַיִת, דְּתַנְיָא: אֲכָלוֹ וְאֵין בּוֹ כְּזַיִת – חַיָּיב, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ כְּזַיִת.
segments.en: The Gemara seeks to clarify the baraita: «But if it» is «obvious to» Rabbi Yehuda that the sciatic nerve from the right thigh is prohibited by Torah law, «why» does he «incur forty» lashes «and nothing more? Let him be flogged eighty» times. The Gemara answers: «Here we are dealing with» a case «where» the volume of one of the sciatic nerves «is not an olive-bulk,» and Rabbi Yehuda holds that in such a case one is not flogged for its consumption. «As it is taught» in a baraita: If «one ate» the entire sciatic nerve «and» its volume «is not an olive-bulk,» he is nevertheless «liable» to be flogged, because he ate a complete, natural unit of forbidden food. «Rabbi Yehuda says:» He is not liable «unless it has» a volume of at least «an olive-bulk.»

segments.he: וְטַעְמָא מַאי? אָמַר רָבָא: אָמַר קְרָא ״הַיָּרֵךְ״ – הַמְיוּמֶּנֶת שֶׁבַּיָּרֵךְ.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And what is the reason» that Rabbi Yehuda holds that only the sciatic nerve of the right thigh is forbidden by Torah law? «Rava said» that it is because the «verse states:» “Therefore the children of Israel eat not the sciatic nerve that is upon the spoon of «the thigh”» (Genesis 32:33). The definite article indicates that this is referring to «the most important thigh.»

segments.he: וְרַבָּנַן, הַהוּא דְּפָשֵׁיט אִיסּוּרֵיהּ בְּכוּלֵּיהּ יָרֵךְ, לְאַפּוֹקֵי חִיצוֹן דְּלָא.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis,» who hold that the sciatic nerves of both the right and left thighs are forbidden by Torah law, explain the definite article as teaching that the prohibition applies to «the one whose prohibition spreads through the entire thigh,» i.e., the inner nerve. This serves «to exclude» the «outer» nerve, «which is not» prohibited by Torah law.

segments.he: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: אָמַר קְרָא ״בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ״ – כְּאָדָם שֶׁחוֹבֵק אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ, וְיָדוֹ מַגַּעַת לְכַף יְמִינוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said» that Rabbi Yehuda holds that the sciatic nerve of the right thigh is forbidden because «the verse states:» “And when he saw that he could not prevail against him, he touched the spoon of his thigh; and the spoon of Jacob’s thigh was strained, «as he wrestled with him”» (Genesis 32:26). The angel grappled with Jacob «like a man who hugs another» in order to throw him to the ground, «and his hand reaches to the spoon of the right» thigh «of the other.»

segments.he: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: כְּגוֹי נִדְמָה לוֹ, דְּאָמַר מָר: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּטְפַּל לוֹ גּוֹי בַּדֶּרֶךְ – טוֹפְלוֹ לִימִינוֹ.
segments.en: «Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani says:» The angel «appeared to him as a gentile, as the Master said: A Jew who is joined by a gentile on the road» and continues his travels with him should «position» the gentile «to his right,» close to one’s dominant hand. This allows the Jew to defend himself against any potential attack. Since Jacob followed this practice, it was therefore Jacob’s right thigh that the angel touched.

segments.he: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַחָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא בַּר עוּלָּא אָמַר: כְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם נִדְמָה לוֹ, דְּאָמַר מָר: הַמְהַלֵּךְ לִימִין רַבּוֹ – הֲרֵי זֶה בּוּר.
segments.en: «Rav Shmuel bar Aḥa said before Rav Pappa in the name of Rava bar Ulla» that the angel «appeared to» Jacob «as a Torah scholar,» and therefore Jacob positioned the angel on his right side, «as the Master said: One who walks to the right of his teacher is an ignoramus,» in that he does not know how to act with good manners. Consequently, it was Jacob’s right thigh that the angel touched.

segments.he: וְרַבָּנַן, מֵאֲחוֹרֵיהּ אֲתָא, וְנַשְּׁיֵיהּ בְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis,» who hold that the sciatic nerves of both thighs are forbidden, understand that the angel «came from behind» Jacob «and hit him on both» thighs.

segments.he: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ״ מַאי דָּרְשִׁי בֵּיהּ? מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לִכְאִידַּךְ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהֶעֱלוּ אֲבַק מַרְגְּלוֹתָם עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד, כְּתִיב הָכָא ״בְּהֵאָבְקוֹ עִמּוֹ״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם ״וְעָנָן אֲבַק רַגְלָיו״.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And the Rabbis, what do they derive» from «this» phrase: «“As he wrestled with him”» (Genesis 32:26)? The Gemara answers: They «require it for the other» interpretation «of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:» This «teaches that the dust [avak] from their feet ascended to the throne of glory. It is written here: “As he wrestled [behe’avko] with him,” and it is written there» in a description of how God will punish the wicked: “The Lord, in the whirlwind and in the storm is His way, «and the clouds are the dust of His feet”» (Nahum 1:3).

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה? שֶׁנָּשָׁה מִמְּקוֹמוֹ וְעָלָה, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״נָשְׁתָה גְבוּרָתָם הָיוּ לְנָשִׁים״.
segments.en: § The Gemara cites another statement of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi concerning the sciatic nerve: «And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: Why is its name called sciatic nerve [gid hanashe]?» It is «because» the sciatic nerve «left [nasha] its place and rose. And similarly» the verse «says:» “The mighty men of Babylon have ceased to fight, they remain in their strongholds; «their might has left [nashata], they are become as women”» (Jeremiah 51:30).

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״דָּבָר שָׁלַח בְּיַעֲקֹב וְנָפַל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״? ״דָּבָר שָׁלַח בְּיַעֲקֹב״ – זֶה גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה, ״וְנָפַל בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ – שֶׁפָּשַׁט אִיסּוּרוֹ בְּכׇל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
segments.en: The Gemara continues with other expositions pertaining to the sciatic nerve. «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: What» is the meaning of that «which is written:» “The Lord «sent a word to Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel”» (Isaiah 9:7)? «“He sent a word to Jacob”; this» is a reference to «the sciatic nerve. “And it has fallen upon Israel”;» this teaches «that its prohibition has» been «extended to the entire Jewish people.»

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״וּטְבוֹחַ טֶבַח וְהָכֵן״? פְּרַע לָהֶן בֵּית הַשְּׁחִיטָה, ״וְהָכֵן״ – טוֹל גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה בִּפְנֵיהֶם, כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר גִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה נֶאֱסָר לִבְנֵי נֹחַ.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina,» also «said: What» is the meaning of that «which is written:» “And when Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house: Bring the men into the house, «and slaughter the animals, and prepare» the meat; for the men shall dine with me at noon” (Genesis 43:16)? Joseph commanded his steward: «Expose the place of the slaughter» on the neck of the animal «to them» so that the brothers will know that it is being slaughtered correctly. «“And prepare”» teaches that Joseph instructed the steward to «remove the sciatic nerve in their presence» so that the brothers would know that it had been fully removed. The Gemara comments that this opinion is «according to the one who said» that «the sciatic nerve was forbidden to» the children of Jacob even before the Torah was given, when they still had the status of «descendants of Noah.»

segments.he: ״וַיִּוָּתֵר יַעֲקֹב לְבַדּוֹ״, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שֶׁנִּשְׁתַּיֵּיר עַל פַּכִּין קְטַנִּים, מִכָּאן לַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁחָבִיב עֲלֵיהֶם מָמוֹנָם יוֹתֵר מִגּוּפָם, וְכׇל כָּךְ לָמָּה? לְפִי שֶׁאֵין פּוֹשְׁטִין יְדֵיהֶן בְּגָזֵל.
segments.en: The Gemara returns to the verse of Jacob wrestling with the angel. The verse states: «“And Jacob was left alone;» and a man wrestled with him until the breaking of the day” (Genesis 32:25). «Rabbi Elazar says:» The reason Jacob remained alone was «that he remained» to collect some «small pitchers» that had been left behind. «From here» it is derived «that the possessions of the righteous are dearer to them than their bodies. And why» do they care «so much» about their possessions? It is «because they do not stretch out their hands to» partake of «stolen property.»

segments.he: ״וַיֵּאָבֵק אִישׁ עִמּוֹ עַד עֲלוֹת הַשָּׁחַר״, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִכָּאן לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁלֹּא יֵצֵא יְחִידִי בַּלַּיְלָה. רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר מֵהָכָא:
segments.en: The verse states: «“And a man wrestled with him until the breaking of the day.” Rabbi Yitzḥak says: From here» it is derived «that a Torah scholar should not go out» of his house «alone at night,» as Jacob went out alone at night and was injured. «Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said» that the source for this instruction is «from here:»

segments.he: ״הִנֵּה הוּא זֹרֶה אֶת גֹּרֶן הַשְּׂעֹרִים״.
segments.en: “And now is there not Boaz our kinsman, whose maidens you were with? «Behold, he winnows barley tonight in the threshing floor»…and it shall be, when he lies down, that you shall mark the place where he shall lie” (Ruth 3:2–3). This teaches that the reason Boaz did not return home from the threshing floor was that a Torah scholar should not go out alone at night.

segments.he: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר וַיַּחֲבֹשׁ אֶת וְגוֹ׳״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Abbahu said» that the source is «from here: “And Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled» his donkey, and took two of his young men with him and Isaac his son; and he split the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went to the place that God had told him” (Genesis 22:3). The fact that Abraham waited until morning and did not set off at night, even though others were traveling with him, indicates that a Torah scholar should not go out at night at all, and certainly not alone.

segments.he: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי מֵהָכָא: ״לֶךְ נָא רְאֵה אֶת שְׁלוֹם אַחֶיךָ וְאֶת שְׁלוֹם וְגוֹ׳״.
segments.en: «And the Rabbis say» that the source is «from here,» the verse that describes when Jacob sent Joseph to his brothers: “And he said to him: «Go now, see whether it is well with you brothers and well» with the flock; and bring me back word. So he sent him out of the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem” (Genesis 37:14). The verse indicates that Jacob sent Joseph at a time when he could see his brothers, i.e., during the day. This shows that a Torah scholar should not go out alone at night.

segments.he: רַב אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״וַיִּזְרַח לוֹ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ״.
segments.en: «Rav said» that the source is «from here: “And the sun rose for him» as he passed over Peniel, and he limped upon his thigh” (Genesis 32:32). This indicates that Jacob remained where he was all night and left in the morning, because a Torah scholar should not go out alone at night.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְאֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בָּאִיטְלִיז שֶׁל אִימָאוּם, שֶׁהָלְכוּ לִיקַּח בְּהֵמָה לְמִשְׁתֵּה בְנוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל. כְּתִיב ״וַיִּזְרַח לוֹ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ״, וְכִי שֶׁמֶשׁ לוֹ לְבַד זָרְחָה? וַהֲלֹא לְכׇל הָעוֹלָם זָרְחָה!
segments.en: The Gemara cites an incident involving the final verse cited above. «Rabbi Akiva says: I asked» the following question of «Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua in the meat market [be’itliz] of» the town «Emmaus, where they went to purchase an animal for the» wedding «feast of Rabban Gamliel’s son: It is written» in the verse: «“And the sun shone for him» when he passed Peniel, and he limped upon his thigh” (Genesis 32:32). «But did the sun shine only for him? Didn’t it shine for the entire world?»

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: שֶׁמֶשׁ הַבָּאָה בַּעֲבוּרוֹ זָרְחָה בַּעֲבוּרוֹ, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיֵּצֵא יַעֲקֹב מִבְּאֵר שָׁבַע וַיֵּלֶךְ חָרָנָה״, וּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּפְגַּע בַּמָּקוֹם״. כִּי מְטָא לְחָרָן אָמַר: אֶפְשָׁר עָבַרְתִּי עַל מָקוֹם שֶׁהִתְפַּלְּלוּ אֲבוֹתַי וַאֲנִי לֹא הִתְפַּלַּלְתִּי? כַּד יָהֵיב דַּעְתֵּיהּ לְמִיהְדַּר, קְפַצָה לֵיהּ אַרְעָא, מִיָּד – ״וַיִּפְגַּע בַּמָּקוֹם״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yitzḥak says:» The verse means that «the sun, which set» early exclusively «for him,» also «shone» early exclusively «for him» in order to rectify the disparity created by the premature sunset. The Gemara explains when the sun set early for him: «As it is written: “And Jacob went out from Beersheba and went toward Haran”» (Genesis 28:10). «And it is written» thereafter: «“And he encountered the place,» and he slept there, because the sun had set” (Genesis 28:11). «When» Jacob «arrived at Haran, he said:» Is it «possible» that «I passed a place where my fathers prayed and I did not pray» there? «When he set his mind to return, the land contracted for him. Immediately» the verse states: «“And he encountered the place,”» indicating that he arrived there miraculously.

segments.he: כַּד צַלִּי, בָּעֵי לְמֶיהְדַּר, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: צַדִּיק זֶה בָּא לְבֵית מְלוֹנִי, וְיִפָּטֵר בְּלֹא לִינָה? מִיָּד, ״בָּא הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ״.
segments.en: «When he» had finished «praying» and «he wanted to return» to Haran, «the Holy One, Blessed be He, said: This righteous man came to my lodging place and he will depart without remaining overnight? Immediately, the sun set» before its proper time so that Jacob would stay overnight in that place.

segments.he: כְּתִיב ״וַיִּקַּח מֵאַבְנֵי הַמָּקוֹם״, וּכְתִיב ״וַיִּקַּח אֶת הָאֶבֶן״. אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁנִּתְקַבְּצוּ כׇּל אוֹתָן אֲבָנִים לְמָקוֹם אֶחָד, וְכׇל אַחַת וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת: ״עָלַי יַנִּיחַ צַדִּיק זֶה רֹאשׁוֹ״. תָּנָא: וְכוּלָּן נִבְלְעוּ בְּאֶחָד.
segments.en: The Gemara cites another exposition of Rabbi Yitzḥak to explain an apparent contradiction between two verses pertaining to this incident. «It is written: “And he took of the stones of the place,» and placed them under his head, and lay down in that place to sleep” (Genesis 28:11). «And it is written:» “And Jacob rose up early in the morning, «and he took the stone» that he had placed under his head, and set it up for a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it” (Genesis 28:18). The first verse indicates that Jacob took several stones, whereas the latter verse indicates that he took only one stone. «Rabbi Yitzḥak says:» This «teaches that all those stones gathered to one place and each one said:» Let «this righteous man place his head upon me.» And it was «taught: And all of them were absorbed into one» large rock.

segments.he: ״וַיַּחֲלֹם וְהִנֵּה סֻלָּם מֻצָּב אַרְצָה״, תָּנָא: כַּמָּה רׇחְבּוֹ שֶׁל סוּלָּם? שְׁמוֹנַת אֲלָפִים פַּרְסָאוֹת, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְהִנֵּה מַלְאֲכֵי אֱלֹהִים עוֹלִים וְיוֹרְדִים בּוֹ״, ״עוֹלִים״ – שְׁנַיִם, ״וְיוֹרְדִים״ – שְׁנַיִם, וְכִי פָגְעוּ בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי הָווּ לְהוּ אַרְבָּעָה.
segments.en: The Gemara expounds other verses pertaining to the same incident. The verse states: «“And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth,» and the top of it reached to heaven; and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it” (Genesis 28:12). It was «taught: How wide was the ladder?» It was «eight thousand parasangs [parsaot], as it is written: “And behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.”» The word «“ascending [olim],”» written in plural, indicates that there were «two» angels ascending simultaneously. Likewise, the term «“and descending [veyordim],”» also in the plural, indicates that «two» angels were descending simultaneously. «And when they met one another they were» a total of «four» in one place, so the ladder must have been wide enough to accommodate four angels.

segments.he: וּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ בְּמַלְאָךְ ״וּגְוִיָּתוֹ כְתַרְשִׁישׁ״, וּגְמִירִי דְּתַרְשִׁישׁ תְּרֵי אַלְפֵי פַּרְסֵי הָוֵי.
segments.en: «And it is written» in a verse «with regard to an angel: “His body was like Tarshish”» (Daniel 10:6). «And» it «is learned» as a tradition «that» the city of «Tarshish was two thousand parasangs.» Consequently, in order to accommodate four angels, the ladder must have been eight thousands parasangs wide.

segments.he: תָּנָא: עוֹלִין וּמִסְתַּכְּלִין בִּדְיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל מַעְלָה, וְיוֹרְדִין וּמִסְתַּכְּלִין בִּדְיוֹקְנוֹ שֶׁל מַטָּה. בְּעוֹ לְסַכּוֹנֵיהּ, מִיָּד ״וְהִנֵּה ה׳ נִצָּב עָלָיו״. אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: אִלְמָלֵא מִקְרָא כָּתוּב אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְאׇמְרוֹ, כְּאָדָם שֶׁמֵּנִיף עַל בְּנוֹ.
segments.en: It was «taught» that the angels were «ascending and gazing at the image of [bidyokeno]» Jacob «above,» engraved on the Throne of Glory, «and descending and gazing at his image below.» The angels subsequently became jealous of Jacob, and «wanted to endanger» his life. «Immediately» Jacob received divine protection, as the verse states: «“And behold, the Lord stood over him”» (Genesis 28:13). «Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: Were it not written» in a «verse it would be impossible to utter it,» in deference to God, since it describes God as standing over Jacob to protect him from the angels «like a man who waves» a fan «over his son» to cool him down.

segments.he: ״הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה שֹׁכֵב עָלֶיהָ וְגוֹ׳״, מַאי רְבוּתֵיהּ? אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁקִּפְּלָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְכׇל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהִנִּיחָה תַּחַת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ, שֶׁתְּהֵא נוֹחָה לִיכָּבֵשׁ לְבָנָיו.
segments.en: The Gemara explains another verse from Jacob’s dream. “And behold, the Lord stood over him and said: I am the Lord, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. «The land upon which you lie,» to you will I give it, and to your seed” (Genesis 28:13). The Gemara asks: «What is the greatness» of this promise, i.e., why is it expressed in this way despite the fact that in a literal sense Jacob was lying on a very small amount of land? «Rabbi Yitzḥak says:» This «teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, folded» up «the entirety of Eretz Yisrael and placed it under Jacob, our patriarch, so that it would be easy for his children to conquer.»

segments.he: ״וַיֹּאמֶר שַׁלְּחֵנִי כִּי עָלָה הַשָּׁחַר״, אָמַר לוֹ: גַּנָּב אַתָּה אוֹ קוּבְיוּסְטוּס אַתָּה שֶׁמִּתְיָירֵא מִן הַשַּׁחַר? אָמַר לוֹ: מַלְאָךְ אֲנִי, וּמִיּוֹם שֶׁנִּבְרֵאתִי לֹא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנִּי לוֹמַר שִׁירָה עַד עַכְשָׁיו.
segments.en: The Gemara returns to the verses that describe Jacob wrestling with the angel. «“And he said: Let me go, for the dawn has risen.» And he said: I will not let you go until you bless me” (Genesis 32:27). Jacob «said to» the angel: «Are you a thief, or are you a gambler [kuveyustus], who is afraid of dawn?» The angel «said to him: I am an angel, and from the day I was created my time to recite a song» before God «has not arrived, until now.» Now I must ascend so that I can sing songs of praise to God.

segments.he: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב, דְּאָמַר רַב חֲנַנְאֵל אָמַר רַב: שָׁלֹשׁ כִּתּוֹת שֶׁל מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹמְרוֹת שִׁירָה בְּכׇל יוֹם, אַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״קָדוֹשׁ״, וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״קָדוֹשׁ״, וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״קָדוֹשׁ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת״.
segments.en: The Gemara comments: This «supports» the opinion «of Rav Ḥananel» when he related what «Rav said. As Rav Ḥananel said» that «Rav said: Three groups of ministering angels recite a song every day» from the verse “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord”; «one says: “Holy,” and» another «one says: “Holy,” and» another «one says: “Holy is the Lord of hosts;» the whole earth is full of His glory” (Isaiah 6:3).

segments.he: מֵיתִיבִי: חֲבִיבִין יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא יוֹתֵר מִמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת, שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה בְּכׇל שָׁעָה, וּמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אֵין אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה אֶלָּא פַּעַם אַחַת בַּיּוֹם, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ פַּעַם אַחַת בְּשַׁבָּת, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ פַּעַם אַחַת בְּחוֹדֶשׁ, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ פַּעַם אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ פַּעַם אַחַת בְּשָׁבוּעַ, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ פַּעַם אַחַת בְּיוֹבֵל, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ פַּעַם אַחַת בָּעוֹלָם.
segments.en: The Gemara «raises an objection» from the following baraita: «The Jewish people are more dear to the Holy One, Blessed be He, than the ministering angels, as the Jewish people» may «recite a song» of praise to God «at any time, but ministering angels recite a song» of praise «only one time per day. And some say» that the ministering angels recite a song of praise «one time per week. And some say» that they recite a song of praise «one time per month. And some say» that they recite a song of praise «one time per year. And some say» that they recite a song of praise «one time in» every «seven years. And some say» that they recite a song of praise «one time per Jubilee. And some say» that they recite a song of praise «one time in» the entire history of «the world.»

segments.he: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מַזְכִּירִין אֶת הַשֵּׁם אַחַר שְׁתֵּי תֵּיבוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ וְגוֹ׳״, וּמַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אֵין מַזְכִּירִין אֶת הַשֵּׁם אֶלָּא לְאַחַר שָׁלֹשׁ תֵּיבוֹת, כְּדִכְתִיב: ״קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת״.
segments.en: «And» furthermore, «the Jewish people mention the name» of God «after two words, as it is stated: “Hear, Israel: The Lord» our God, the Lord is one” (Deuteronomy 6:4). «But the ministering angels mention the name» of God «only after three words, as it is written:» “And one called unto another, and said: «“Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts;» the whole earth is full of His glory” (Isaiah 6:3).

segments.he: וְאֵין מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה לְמַעְלָה, עַד שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמַטָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בְּרׇן יַחַד כּוֹכְבֵי בֹקֶר״, וַהֲדַר ״וַיָּרִיעוּ כׇּל בְּנֵי אֱלֹהִים״.
segments.en: «And the ministering angels do not recite» their «song above until the Jewish people recite» their song «below,» on earth, «as it is stated: “When the morning stars sang together”» (Job 38:7), referring to the Jewish people, who are compared to stars; «and» only «then» does the verse state: «“And all the sons of God shouted for joy,”» which is a reference to the angels. This baraita teaches that the angels mention the name of God only after three words, i.e., after saying the word “holy” three times, whereas according to what Rav Ḥananel stated that Rav said, the third group of angels says the word “holy” once and then immediately mentions the name of God.

segments.he: אֶלָּא, אַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״קָדוֹשׁ״, וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ״, וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ קָדוֹשׁ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת״. וְהָאִיכָּא ״בָּרוּךְ״!
segments.en: The Gemara emends Rav Ḥananel’s statement citing Rav: «Rather,» Rav said that «one» group of ministering angels «says: “Holy,” and» another «one says: “Holy, holy,” and» another «one says: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts.”» The Gemara challenges the statement of the baraita that the angels mention the name of God only after three words: «But there is» the verse: “Then a spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great rushing: «Blessed be» the glory of the Lord from His place” (Ezekiel 3:12). In this praise, “Blessed be the glory of the Lord,” the word “Lord” appears as the third Hebrew word, apparently uttered by the ministering angels.

segments.he: ״בָּרוּךְ״ – אוֹפַנִּים הוּא דְּאָמְרִי לֵיהּ. וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כֵּיוָן דְּאִתְיְהִיב רְשׁוּתָא, אִתְיְהִיב.
segments.en: The Gemara answers that it is the «ofanim who say» the verse: «“Blessed be» the glory of the Lord from His place,” as the next verse mentions “the noise of the ofanim” (Ezekiel 3:13), and Rav Ḥanina’s statement citing Rav was referring not to ofanim but to ministering angels. «And if you wish, say» that «once permission has been given» to them to mention the name of God after three words when they say: “Holy, holy, holy,” permission is also «given» to them to mention the name of God again while praising Him even after fewer than three words.

segments.he: ״וַיָּשַׂר אֶל מַלְאָךְ וַיֻּכָל בָּכָה וַיִּתְחַנֶּן לוֹ״ – אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מִי נַעֲשָׂה שַׂר לְמִי, כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״כִּי שָׂרִיתָ עִם אֱלֹהִים״ – הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר יַעֲקֹב נַעֲשָׂה שַׂר לַמַּלְאָךְ.
segments.en: The Gemara continues to discuss Jacob wrestling with the angel. The prophet states: «“So he strove [vayyasar] with an angel, and prevailed; he wept, and made supplication to him;» at Beth El he would find him, and there he would speak with us” (Hosea 12:5). From this verse «I do not know who became master [sar],» i.e., was victorious, «over whom. When» another verse «states:» “And he said: Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel; «for you have striven with angels» and with men, and have prevailed” (Genesis 32:29), «you must say» that «Jacob became master over the angel.»

segments.he: ״בָּכָה וַיִּתְחַנֶּן לוֹ״ – אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מִי בָּכָה לְמִי, כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״וַיֹּאמֶר שַׁלְּחֵנִי״, הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: מַלְאָךְ בָּכָה לְיַעֲקֹב.
segments.en: The verse in Hosea states: «“He wept, and made supplication to him.”» From this verse «I do not know who cried to whom. When» another verse «states: “And he said: Let me go,» for the dawn has risen” (Genesis 32:27), «you must say» that «the angel cried to Jacob.»

segments.he: ״כִּי שָׂרִיתָ עִם אֱלֹהִים וְעִם אֲנָשִׁים״, אָמַר רַבָּה: רֶמֶז רָמַז לוֹ שֶׁעֲתִידִים שְׁנֵי שָׂרִים לָצֵאת מִמֶּנּוּ, רֹאשׁ גּוֹלָה שֶׁבְּבָבֶל וְנָשִׂיא שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, מִכָּאן רָמַז לוֹ גָּלוּת.
segments.en: The verse states: “And he said: Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel; «for you have striven with angels [elohim] and with men,» and have prevailed” (Genesis 32:29). «Rabba says:» The angel «intimated to» Jacob «that in the future two princes would emerge from him:» They are the «Exilarch who is in Babylonia and the Nasi who is in Eretz Yisrael.» And «from here he» also «intimated to» Jacob that there would be «an exile.»

segments.he: ״וּבַגֶּפֶן שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׂרִיגִים״, אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב: אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׂרֵי גֵּאִים הַיּוֹצְאִים מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּכׇל דּוֹר וָדוֹר, פְּעָמִים שֶׁשְּׁנַיִם כָּאן וְאֶחָד בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, פְּעָמִים שֶׁשְּׁנַיִם בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאֶחָד כָּאן. יְהִיבוּ רַבָּנַן עֵינַיְיהוּ בְּרַבָּנָא עוּקְבָא וְרַבָּנָא נְחֶמְיָה בְּנֵי בְרַתֵּיה דְּרַב.
segments.en: Similarly, with regard to the dream of Pharaoh’s butler, the verse states: «“And in the vine were three branches [sarigim];» and as it was budding, its blossoms shot forth, and its clusters brought forth ripe grapes” (Genesis 40:10). «Rav Ḥiyya bar Abba says» that «Rav says: These» three branches refer to the «three proud princes [sarei ge’im] who emerge from the Jewish people in each and every generation.» There are «times» when «two are here» in Babylonia «and one is in Eretz Yisrael,» and there are «times» when «two are in Eretz Yisrael and one is here» in Babylonia. When this was stated in the study hall, «the Sages» present «turned their eyes toward Rabbana Ukva and Rabbana Neḥemya, the sons of the daughter of Rav,» who were from the family of the Exilarch and were two leaders of the generation who resided in Babylonia.

segments.he: רָבָא אָמַר: אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׂרֵי גוֹיִם, שֶׁמְלַמְּדִים זְכוּת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכׇל דּוֹר וָדוֹר.
segments.en: «Rava says» a different explanation of the verse: «These» three branches [sarigim] «are the three ministering» angels appointed to oversee «the gentiles [sarei goyim], who plead in favor of the Jewish people in each and every generation.»

segments.he: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: ״גֶּפֶן״ – זֶה הָעוֹלָם, ״שְׁלֹשָׁה שְׂרִיגִים״ – זֶה אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב, ״וְהִיא כְפֹרַחַת עָלְתָה נִצָּהּ״ – אֵלּוּ הָאִמָּהוֹת, ״הִבְשִׁילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶיהָ עֲנָבִים״ – אֵלּוּ הַשְּׁבָטִים.
segments.en: «It is taught» in a baraita: «Rabbi Eliezer says» an alternate interpretation of the verse. «“Vine”; this» is a reference to «the world. “Three branches”; this» is a reference to «Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. “And as it was budding, its blossoms shot forth”; these are the matriarchs. “And its clusters brought forth ripe grapes”; these are the» twelve «tribes,» i.e., the twelve sons of Jacob.

segments.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וְכִי מַרְאִין לוֹ לְאָדָם מַה שֶּׁהָיָה? וַהֲלֹא אֵין מַרְאִין לוֹ לְאָדָם אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁעָתִיד לִהְיוֹת! אֶלָּא ״גֶּפֶן״ – זֶה תּוֹרָה, ״שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׂרִיגִים״ – אֵלּוּ מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וּמִרְיָם, ״וְהִיא כְפֹרַחַת עָלְתָה נִצָּהּ״ – אֵלּוּ סַנְהֶדְרִין, ״הִבְשִׁילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶיהָ עֲנָבִים״ – אֵלּוּ הַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁבְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: But is a person shown» in a dream «what was» in the past? «Isn’t» it true that «one is shown only what will be in the future?» Since the patriarchs, matriarchs, and sons of Jacob were all born prior to this dream, the dream was not alluding to them. «Rather,» the verse should be interpreted as follows: «“Vine”; this» is a reference to «the Torah. “Three branches”; these are Moses, Aaron, and Miriam. “And as it was budding, its blossoms shot forth”; these are the» members of the «Sanhedrin. “And its clusters brought forth ripe grapes”; these are the righteous» people «who» live «in each and every generation.»

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: עֲדַיִין צְרִיכִין אָנוּ לַמּוֹדָעִי, דְּמוֹקֵים לֵיהּ כּוּלֵּיהּ בְּחַד מָקוֹם. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַמּוֹדָעִי אוֹמֵר: ״גֶּפֶן״ – זֶה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם, ״שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׂרִיגִים״ – זֶה מִקְדָּשׁ, מֶלֶךְ, וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, ״וְהִיא כְפֹרַחַת עָלְתָה נִצָּהּ״ – אֵלּוּ פִּרְחֵי כְהוּנָּה, ״הִבְשִׁילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶיהָ עֲנָבִים״ – אֵלּוּ נְסָכִים.
segments.en: «Rabban Gamliel said:» In order to understand this verse (Genesis 40:10) «we still need» the explanation «of» Rabbi Elazar «HaModa’i, who» is an expert in matters of aggada, as he «interprets all of» the phrases in the verse as referring to «one location. Rabbi Elazar HaModa’i says: “Vine”; this» is a reference to «Jerusalem. “Three branches”; this» is a reference to the «Temple,» the «king and» the «High Priest. “And as it was budding [poraḥat], its blossoms shot forth”; these are the young priests [pirḥei khehunna]. “And its clusters brought forth ripe grapes”; these are the» wine «libations.»

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּמַתָּנוֹת, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: ״גֶּפֶן״ – זוֹ תּוֹרָה, ״שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׂרִיגִים״ – זֶה בְּאֵר, עַמּוּד עָנָן, וּמָן, ״וְהִיא כְפֹרַחַת עָלְתָה נִצָּהּ״ – אֵלּוּ הַבִּכּוּרִים, ״הִבְשִׁילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶיהָ עֲנָבִים״ – אֵלּוּ נְסָכִים.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi interprets it with» reference to the «gifts» that God gave the Jewish people, «as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: “Vine”; this» is a reference to the «Torah. “Three branches”; this» is a reference to the miraculous items that accompanied the Jewish people in the wilderness and sustained and protected them: The «well, the pillar of cloud, and the manna. “And as it was budding, its blossoms shot forth”; these are the first fruits» that are brought to the Temple. «“And its clusters brought forth ripe grapes”; these are» the wine «libations.»

segments.he: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: ״גֶּפֶן״ – אֵלּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״גֶּפֶן מִמִּצְרַיִם תַּסִּיעַ״. ״שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׂרִיגִים״ – אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה רְגָלִים שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹלִין בָּהֶן בְּכׇל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה. ״וְהִיא כְפֹרַחַת עָלְתָה נִצָּהּ״ – הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְרוֹת וְלִרְבּוֹת, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל פָּרוּ וַיִּשְׁרְצוּ״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says: “Vine”; this» is a reference to «the Jewish people, and similarly» another verse «states: “You plucked up a vine out of Egypt;» You drove out the nations and planted it” (Psalms 80:9). «“Three branches”; these are the three» pilgrimage «Festivals, on which the Jewish people ascend» to Jerusalem «every year. “And as it was budding, its blossoms shot forth,”» means that «the time has arrived for the Jewish people to be fruitful and multiply, and similarly» another verse «states: “And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly,» and multiplied, and became exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them” (Exodus 1:7).

segments.he: ״עָלְתָה נִצָּה״ – הִגִּיעַ זְמַן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לִיגָּאֵל, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וְיֵז נִצְחָם עַל בְּגָדַי וְכׇל מַלְבּוּשַׁי אֶגְאָלְתִּי״, ״הִבְשִׁילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶיהָ עֲנָבִים״ – הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם לִשְׁתּוֹת כּוֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָה.
segments.en: «“Its blossoms [nitzah] shot forth”» means that «the time has arrived for the Jewish people to be redeemed. And similarly» another verse «states: “And their eternity [nitzḥam] is dashed against My garments, and I have redeemed all My raiment”» (Isaiah 63:3). «“And its clusters brought forth ripe grapes”» means that «the time has arrived for Egypt to drink the cup of fury,» i.e., to receive its punishment.

segments.he: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רָבָא: שְׁלֹשָׁה כּוֹסוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בְּמִצְרַיִם לָמָה? אֶחָד, שֶׁשָּׁתָת בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה, וְאֶחָד שֶׁשָּׁתָת בִּימֵי פַּרְעֹה נְכֹה, וְאֶחָד שֶׁעֲתִידָה לִשְׁתּוֹת עִם כׇּל הַגּוֹיִם.
segments.en: «And this is as Rava said: Why» are there «three cups stated with regard to Egypt» in the dream of Pharaoh’s butler (see Genesis 40:11)? They are an allusion to three cups of misfortune that would later befall Egypt: «One that» Egypt «drank in the days of Moses» during the ten plagues and the Exodus; «one that» Egypt «drank in the days of Pharaoh Nekho,» the king of Egypt defeated by Nebuchadnezzar; «and one that» Egypt «will drink in the future with all the» other «nations,» when they are punished in the time of the Messiah.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא: כִּי דָרֵישׁ לְהוּ רַב לְהָנֵי קְרָאֵי בְּאַגַּדְתָּא, כְּוָותָךְ דָּרֵישׁ לְהוּ.
segments.en: «Rabbi Abba said to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba: When Rav interpreted these verses homiletically he interpreted them according to» the way in which «you» have interpreted them, and not according to any of the other opinions cited above.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: אוּמָּה זוֹ כְּגֶפֶן נִמְשְׁלָה. זְמוֹרוֹת שֶׁבָּהּ – אֵלּוּ בַּעֲלֵי בָתִּים, אֶשְׁכּוֹלוֹת שֶׁבָּהּ – אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, עָלִין שֶׁבָּהּ – אֵלּוּ עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ, קְנוֹקָנוֹת שֶׁבָּהּ – אֵלּוּ רֵיקָנִים שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
segments.en: Similar to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba’s interpretation of the word vine as an allusion to the Jewish people, «Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: This nation is likened to a vine. The branches of» the vine support the clusters of grapes, the leaves, and the tendrils; «these are» represented among the Jewish people by «the homeowners,» who provide financial support for the entire nation. «The clusters» of grapes «on» the vine, «these are the Torah scholars. The leaves on» the vine, which protect the grapes, «these are the ignoramuses,» who protect the Torah scholars. «The tendrils of» the vine, which do not directly serve the grapes themselves, «these are the empty» ones «of the Jewish people.»

segments.he: וְהַיְינוּ דִּשְׁלַחוּ מִתָּם: לִיבְעֵי רַחֲמִים אִיתְכָּלַיָּא עַל עָלַיָּא, דְּאִילְמָלֵא עָלַיָּא לָא מִתְקַיְּימָן אִיתְכָּלַיָּא.
segments.en: «And this is» the meaning of the instruction «that they sent from there,» i.e., from Eretz Yisrael: «Let the clusters» of grapes «pray for the leaves, as were it not for the leaves, the clusters» of grapes «would not survive.»

segments.he: ״וָאֶכְּרֶהָ לִּי בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר כָּסֶף״, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק: אֵין ״כִּירָה״ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן מְכִירָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״בְּקִבְרִי אֲשֶׁר כָּרִיתִי לִי״.
segments.en: § The Gemara cites homiletical interpretations of other verses that pertain to the leaders of the Jewish people in Eretz Yisrael and Babylonia. The verse states: «“So I bought her [va’ekkereha] to me for fifteen pieces of silver,» and a ḥomer of barley, and a half-ḥomer of barley” (Hosea 3:2). «Rabbi Yoḥanan says in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:» The term «kira,» which forms the basis of the verb va’ekkereha, «is nothing other than language» referring to «a sale [mekhira], as it is stated» that Joseph said: “My father made me swear, saying: Lo, I die; «in my grave that I have acquired [kariti] for me» in the land of Canaan, there shall you bury me” (Genesis 50:5).

segments.he: ״בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר״ – זֶה חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּנִיסָן שֶׁבּוֹ נִגְאֲלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם, ״כָּסֶף״ – אֵלּוּ צַדִּיקִים, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר ״צְרוֹר הַכֶּסֶף לָקַח בְּיָדוֹ״.
segments.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan continues: «“For fifteen» pieces of silver”; «this» is a reference to «the fifteenth of Nisan,» the date «on which the Jewish people were redeemed from Egypt. “Silver”; these are the righteous» people. «And similarly,» another verse «states: “He has taken the bag of silver with him”» (Proverbs 7:20), a reference to God taking the righteous away prior to the destruction of the First Temple (see Sanhedrin 96b).

segments.he: ״חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים וְלֶתֶךְ שְׂעוֹרִים״ – אֵלּוּ אַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה צַדִּיקִים שֶׁהָעוֹלָם מִתְקַיֵּים בָּהֶם, וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם שְׁלֹשִׁים כָּאן וַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאִם שְׁלֹשִׁים בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר כָּאן. כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וָאֶקְחָה שְׁלֹשִׁים הַכֶּסֶף וָאַשְׁלִיךְ אֹתוֹ בֵּית ה׳ אֶל הַיּוֹצֵר״ – הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: שְׁלֹשִׁים בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר כָּאן.
segments.en: The verse states: «“A ḥomer of barley, and a half-ḥomer of barley.”» A ḥomer equals thirty se’a, and a half-ḥomer equals fifteen se’a, totaling forty-five se’a; «these are the forty-five righteous» individuals «in whose» merit «the world» continues to «exist. And» although the verse alludes to the fact that thirty of these righteous individuals are in one place and fifteen are elsewhere, «I do not know if thirty are here» in Babylonia «and fifteen are in Eretz Yisrael, or if thirty are in Eretz Yisrael and fifteen are here» in Babylonia. «When it says» in a different verse: «“And I took the thirty pieces of silver and cast them into the treasury, in the house of the Lord”» (Zechariah 11:13), «you must say» that «thirty» of the righteous individuals are «in Eretz Yisrael and fifteen are here» in Babylonia.

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְרוּבַּיְיהוּ מִשְׁתַּכְחִי בְּבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא דְּתוּתֵי אַפְּתָא, וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: ״וָאֹמַר אֲלֵיהֶם אִם טוֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶם הָבוּ שְׂכָרִי וְאִם לֹא חֲדָלוּ וַיִּשְׁקְלוּ אֶת שְׂכָרִי שְׁלֹשִׁים כָּסֶף״.
segments.en: «Abaye said: And most of the» fifteen righteous individuals in Babylonia «are found in the synagogue under the upper room. And this is» the meaning of that «which is written: “And I said to them: If it is good in your eyes, give me my hire; and if not, refrain. And they weighed for my hire thirty pieces of silver”» (Zechariah 11:12).

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשִׁים צַדִּיקֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם, שֶׁאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם מִתְקַיְּימִים עֲלֵיהֶם. עוּלָּא אָמַר: אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשִׁים מִצְוֹת שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ עֲלֵיהֶם בְּנֵי נֹחַ, וְאֵין מְקַיְּימִין אֶלָּא שְׁלֹשָׁה. אַחַת
segments.en: «Rabbi Yehuda says: These are the thirty righteous» individuals among the «nations of the world, in whose» merit «the nations of the world» continue to «exist. Ulla says: These are the thirty mitzvot that the descendants of Noah» initially «accepted upon themselves; but they fulfill only three» of them. «One» of these three mitzvot is

segments.he: שֶׁאֵין כּוֹתְבִין כְּתוּבָּה לִזְכָרִים, וְאַחַת שֶׁאֵין שׁוֹקְלִין בְּשַׂר הַמֵּת בְּמָקוֹלִין, וְאַחַת שֶׁמְּכַבְּדִין אֶת הַתּוֹרָה.
segments.en: «that they do not write a marriage contract for» a wedding between two «males;» although they violate the prohibition against engaging in homosexuality, they are not so brazen as to write a marriage contract as for a regular marriage. «And one» of the three mitzvot is «that» although they are suspected of eating human beings, «they do not weigh the flesh of the dead in butcher shops» [«bemakkulin»] and sell it publicly; «and one» is «that they honor the Torah.»

moves.cueHe: איבעיא להו
moves.summary: asks whether Rabbi Yehuda's דעת is the settled logic of the Torah or an inclination of reason under uncertainty
moves.about: whether Rabbi Yehuda's דעת means the Torah's settled logic (only the right thigh is forbidden) or an inclination of reason under uncertainty which thigh it is

moves.cueHe: והוינן בה: הני גידי מאי עבידתייהו
moves.summary: recalls the earlier discussion: which sinews can the mishna mean
moves.about: which sinews of the Paschal offering the mishna can mean, given that edible ones should be eaten and uneaten ones are simply leftover

moves.cueHe: אי גידי בשר
moves.summary: floats that the sinews are flesh-sinews, or else simply leftover meat
moves.about: the mishna's sinews are neck sinews, which is why they are listed separately

moves.cueHe: ליכלינהו
moves.summary: knocks both floats down: edible ones should be eaten, leftover ones are already covered
moves.about: rejecting the floated readings that the mishna's sinews are flesh-sinews or are simply leftover meat

moves.cueHe: אלא גידי צואר
moves.summary: settles that the mishna means the hard neck sinews
moves.about: deploying the Pesahim mishna as a candidate resolution of the standing dilemma about Rabbi Yehuda

moves.cueHe: אי לאו בשר נינהו – לישדינהו
moves.summary: presses that neck sinews, not being meat, should simply be discarded
moves.about: if neck sinews are not meat they should simply be discarded rather than burned on the sixteenth

moves.cueHe: תא שמע
moves.summary: brings the Pesahim mishna that bones, sinews and leftover are burned on the sixteenth, as a candidate resolution
moves.about: bringing the mishna that the bones, sinews and leftover of the Paschal offering are burned on the sixteenth

moves.cueHe: ואמר רב חסדא: לא נצרכה אלא לגיד הנשה
moves.summary: answers that the clause is needed for the sciatic nerve, taught according to Rabbi Yehuda
moves.about: the mishna's mention of sinews is needed only for the sciatic nerve

moves.cueHe: אי אמרת בשלמא ספוקי מספקא ליה – שפיר
moves.summary: lands the proof on the dilemma: only uncertainty explains why both nerves are burned
moves.about: the horn of the dilemma that Rabbi Yehuda is certain cannot explain why both sciatic nerves are burned rather than one eaten and one discarded

moves.cueHe: לעולם אימא לך מיפשט פשיטא ליה
moves.summary: pushes the proof away by reading the mishna of nerves identified and then intermingled
moves.about: how the burning of both nerves is compatible with Rabbi Yehuda being certain that only the right thigh is forbidden

moves.cueHe: רב אשי אמר: לא נצרכה אלא לשמנו
moves.summary: pushes the proof away by referring the mishna's sinews to the fat around the nerve
moves.about: whether the Pesahim mishna bears at all on the dilemma about Rabbi Yehuda's certainty

moves.cueHe: רבינא אמר: לא נצרכה אלא לכדרב יהודה אמר שמואל
moves.summary: pushes the proof away by referring the mishna's sinews to Shmuel's outer nerve
moves.about: whether the Pesahim mishna bears at all on the dilemma about Rabbi Yehuda's certainty

moves.cueHe: תא שמע
moves.summary: brings the mishna of 96a on eating an olive-bulk from each nerve as a second candidate resolution
moves.about: bringing the mishna on one who eats an olive-bulk from each of the two sciatic nerves

moves.cueHe: אי אמרת בשלמא מיפשט פשיטא ליה – שפיר
moves.summary: argues that on the uncertainty horn each forewarning is an uncertain one, which Rabbi Yehuda rejects
moves.about: citing Rabbi Yehuda's position that an uncertain forewarning is not a forewarning

moves.cueHe: דתניא
moves.summary: cites the baraita of striking two men, showing Rabbi Yehuda exempts on uncertain forewarning
moves.about: the baraita on one who struck or cursed two men, one of whom is certainly his father

moves.cueHe: האי תנא סבר לה כאידך תנא דרבי יהודה
moves.summary: answers that the tanna of 96a follows the other tradition, on which Rabbi Yehuda accepts uncertain forewarning
moves.about: how the mishna at 96a can hold one liable for both nerves even if Rabbi Yehuda is uncertain — its tanna follows the other tradition of Rabbi Yehuda

moves.cueHe: דתניא
moves.summary: cites the baraita on לא תותירו to document that other tradition of Rabbi Yehuda
moves.about: the baraita on לא תותירו, in which Rabbi Yehuda holds one is not flogged for leaving over the Paschal offering

moves.cueHe: רבי יעקב אומר: לא מן השם הוא זה
moves.summary: replaces Rabbi Yehuda's reason with a different one: a prohibition with no action carries no lashes
moves.about: why one is not flogged for leaving over the Paschal offering — because the prohibition is rectified by a positive mitzva, or because it involves no action

moves.cueHe: תא שמע
moves.summary: brings the baraita of two nerves from two thighs of two animals as a third candidate resolution
moves.about: bringing the baraita on eating two sciatic nerves from two thighs of two animals

moves.cueHe: מדקאמר משתי ירכות משתי בהמות
moves.summary: concludes and affirms: both nerves are right-thigh nerves, so Rabbi Yehuda is certain
moves.about: since the baraita specifies two thighs of two animals, both nerves are right-thigh nerves and certainly forbidden — proving Rabbi Yehuda is certain

moves.cueHe: ואי פשיטא ליה, אמאי סופג ארבעים ותו לא
moves.summary: presses that certainty should yield eighty lashes, not forty
moves.about: if Rabbi Yehuda is certain both nerves are forbidden, why does he impose only forty lashes rather than eighty

moves.cueHe: הכא במאי עסקינן – כגון דלית בו כזית
moves.summary: answers that one of the two nerves was smaller than an olive-bulk
moves.about: the baraita speaks of a case where one of the two nerves is smaller than an olive-bulk

moves.cueHe: דתניא
moves.summary: cites the baraita in which Rabbi Yehuda requires an olive-bulk for liability
moves.about: the baraita on eating a whole sciatic nerve that is less than an olive-bulk

moves.cueHe: וטעמא מאי
moves.summary: asks the ground of Rabbi Yehuda's restriction to the right thigh
moves.about: the reason Rabbi Yehuda holds that only the sciatic nerve of the right thigh is forbidden by Torah law

moves.cueHe: אמר רבא: אמר קרא ״הירך״
moves.summary: answers from the definite article of ״הירך״ — the dominant thigh
moves.about: the scriptural reason for Rabbi Yehuda's restriction of the prohibition to the right thigh

moves.cueHe: ורבנן, ההוא דפשיט איסוריה בכוליה ירך
moves.summary: reads the same word as excluding the outer nerve rather than the left thigh
moves.about: for the Rabbis ״הירך״ points to the nerve whose prohibition spreads through the whole thigh, excluding the outer nerve

moves.cueHe: ורבי יהושע בן לוי אמר: אמר קרא ״בהאבקו עמו״
moves.summary: supplies a rival derivation for Rabbi Yehuda from the wrestling as a hug
moves.about: bringing ״בהאבקו עמו״ as the source that it was Jacob's right thigh that was struck

moves.cueHe: רבי שמואל בר נחמני אמר: כגוי נדמה לו
moves.summary: derives the right thigh from the angel appearing as a gentile, whom one places on one's right
moves.about: why it was specifically Jacob's right thigh that the angel struck

moves.cueHe: רב שמואל בר אחא קמיה דרב פפא משמיה דרבא בר עולא אמר
moves.summary: derives it from the angel appearing as a Torah scholar, to whose left one walks

moves.cueHe: ורבנן, מאחוריה אתא ונשייה בתרוייהו
moves.summary: the Rabbis answer that the angel came from behind and struck both thighs
moves.about: whether the Torah prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies to the nerves of both thighs or only to the right one

moves.cueHe: ורבנן, האי ״בהאבקו עמו״ מאי דרשי ביה
moves.summary: asks what the Rabbis then derive from ״בהאבקו עמו״
moves.about: what the Rabbis, who hold the angel came from behind, derive from ״בהאבקו עמו״

moves.cueHe: מבעי ליה לכאידך דרבי יהושע בן לוי
moves.summary: answers that they need it for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's other exposition, on the dust reaching the throne
moves.about: the Rabbis need ״בהאבקו עמו״ for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's other exposition, on the dust reaching the throne of glory

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי יהושע בן לוי: למה נקרא שמו גיד הנשה
moves.summary: a further teaching of his on the sciatic nerve: it is so called because it slipped from its place
moves.about: why the sinew is called gid hanashe — because it slipped (nasha) from its place and rose

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: מאי דכתיב ״דבר שלח ביעקב״
moves.summary: opens a new run of expositions on the sciatic nerve: the word sent to Jacob fell upon all Israel
moves.about: the word sent to Jacob is the sciatic nerve, and its falling upon Israel is the spread of its prohibition to all Israel

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: מאי דכתיב ״וטבוח טבח והכן״
moves.summary: reads Joseph's order as exposing the slaughter and removing the nerve before the brothers
moves.about: Joseph's order to slaughter and prepare means exposing the place of slaughter and removing the sciatic nerve before the brothers

moves.cueHe: כמאן דאמר גיד הנשה נאסר לבני נח
moves.summary: notes that the exposition presupposes the view that the nerve was already forbidden to Noahides
moves.about: which view Rabbi Yosei's exposition presupposes — that the sciatic nerve was already forbidden to the descendants of Noah

moves.cueHe: ״ויותר יעקב לבדו״, אמר רבי אלעזר
moves.summary: opens the aggadic run on Jacob's night alone: he went back for small pitchers
moves.about: Jacob remained alone because he went back for small pitchers he had left behind

moves.cueHe: ״ויאבק איש עמו עד עלות השחר״, אמר רבי יצחק
moves.summary: derives from the same night that a Torah scholar should not go out alone at night
moves.about: that a Torah scholar should not go out alone at night, since Jacob did so and was injured

moves.cueHe: רבי אבא בר כהנא אמר מהכא
moves.summary: offers Boaz at the threshing floor as the source instead
moves.about: bringing Boaz winnowing barley at night as the source that a Torah scholar should not go out alone at night

moves.cueHe: ״הנה הוא זורה את גורן השעורים״
moves.summary: gives the verse itself
moves.about: which verse is the source of the rule that a Torah scholar should not go out alone at night — a question to which Rabbi Abbahu, the Rabbis and Rav each add a further verse

moves.cueHe: רבי אבהו אמר מהכא
moves.summary: offers Abraham rising early as the source
moves.about: bringing Abraham rising early in the morning as the source of the rule

moves.cueHe: ורבנן אמרי מהכא
moves.summary: offer Jacob sending Joseph by daylight as the source
moves.about: bringing Jacob's sending Joseph to see his brothers' welfare as the source of the rule

moves.cueHe: רב אמר מהכא: ״ויזרח לו השמש״
moves.summary: offers Jacob leaving only at sunrise as the source
moves.about: bringing ״ויזרח לו השמש״ as the source that Jacob waited for daylight

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי עקיבא: שאלתי את רבן גמליאל ואת רבי יהושע
moves.summary: reports asking his masters why the verse says the sun shone for Jacob alone
moves.about: why the verse says the sun shone for Jacob alone, when it shines for the whole world

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יצחק: שמש הבאה בעבורו זרחה בעבורו
moves.summary: answers that the sun which had set early for him also rose early for him
moves.about: why the verse singles out Jacob — the sun that had set early for him also rose early for him

moves.cueHe: כד צלי, בעי למיהדר
moves.summary: narrates why the sun set early: God would not let the righteous man leave without lodging

moves.cueHe: כתיב ״ויקח מאבני המקום״, וכתיב ״ויקח את האבן״
moves.summary: sets the plural stones of one verse against the single stone of the other
moves.about: whether Jacob took several stones or a single stone for his head

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יצחק: מלמד שנתקבצו כל אותן אבנים למקום אחד
moves.summary: resolves it: the stones gathered, each asking to hold the righteous man's head
moves.about: the many stones gathered to one place, each asking that the righteous man rest his head on it

moves.cueHe: תנא: וכולן נבלעו באחד
moves.summary: a tannaitic addition: all of them were absorbed into one
moves.about: the tannaitic teaching that all the stones were absorbed into one

moves.cueHe: תנא: כמה רחבו של סולם
moves.summary: opens the expositions of the ladder: it was eight thousand parasangs wide
moves.about: bringing the plural forms olim and yordim to establish that four angels met on the ladder

moves.cueHe: וכתיב ביה במלאך ״וגויתו כתרשיש״
moves.summary: supplies the measure of a single angel to fix the ladder's width
moves.about: bringing the angel's body being like Tarshish to fix the measure of each angel

moves.cueHe: תנא: עולין ומסתכלין בדיוקנו של מעלה
moves.summary: the angels compared Jacob's image above and below and sought to endanger him, and God stood over him
moves.about: bringing ״והנה ה׳ נצב עליו״ as God's protection of Jacob from the jealous angels

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש: אלמלא מקרא כתוב אי אפשר לאמרו
moves.summary: glosses God's standing over Jacob as a man fanning his son, sayable only because scripture says it
moves.about: the verse's image of God standing over Jacob is one that could not be uttered were it not written

moves.cueHe: מאי רבותיה
moves.summary: asks what is great about promising Jacob only the ground he lies on
moves.about: what is great about promising Jacob the land upon which he lies, which is only a small patch

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יצחק: מלמד שקפלה הקדוש ברוך הוא לכל ארץ ישראל
moves.summary: answers that all of Eretz Yisrael was folded up beneath him
moves.about: God folded up the whole of Eretz Yisrael and placed it under Jacob so it would be easy for his children to conquer

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: גנב אתה או קוביוסטוס אתה
moves.summary: Jacob asks the angel why he fears the dawn
moves.about: why the angel must leave at dawn — is he a thief or a gambler who fears daylight

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: מלאך אני
moves.summary: the angel answers that his turn to sing before God has come for the first time
moves.about: why the angel must leave at dawn — his turn to recite song before God has come for the first time

moves.cueHe: מסייע ליה לרב חננאל אמר רב
moves.summary: notes that the angel's answer supports Rav Hananel's report of Rav on the three groups of angels
moves.about: whether each group of ministering angels recites song only once, so that this angel had never yet sung

moves.cueHe: מיתיבי
moves.summary: objects from the baraita that Israel are dearer than the angels, who sing but rarely
moves.about: whether the third group of angels mentions God's name after only one word of קדוש, as Rav Hananel reported in Rav's name

moves.cueHe: וישראל מזכירין את השם אחר שתי תיבות
moves.summary: the baraita continues: Israel name God after two words, the angels only after three
moves.about: bringing שמע ישראל to show that Israel mention God's name after only two words

moves.cueHe: ואין מלאכי השרת אומרים שירה למעלה
moves.summary: and the angels do not sing above until Israel sing below — completing the objection
moves.about: bringing ברן יחד כוכבי בקר to show Israel sing below before the angels sing above

moves.cueHe: אלא, אחת אומרת ״קדוש״
moves.summary: restates Rav Hananel's report so that the third group says קדוש three times before the name
moves.about: how Rav Hananel's report of Rav must be restated so that the angels still say קדוש three times before the name

moves.cueHe: והאיכא ״ברוך״
moves.summary: presses that ברוך כבוד ה׳ names God after only two words
moves.about: whether angels ever mention God's name after fewer than three words, as ברוך כבוד ה׳ appears to show

moves.cueHe: ״ברוך״ – אופנים הוא דאמרי ליה
moves.summary: answers that the ofanim, not the ministering angels, say it
moves.about: who says ברוך כבוד ה׳ — it is the ofanim, not the ministering angels of the baraita

moves.cueHe: ואיבעית אימא: כיון דאתיהיב רשותא
moves.summary: a second answer: once permission was given it was given for fewer words too
moves.about: once permission to mention the name after three words was given, it was given for fewer as well

moves.cueHe: ״וישר אל מלאך ויוכל בכה ויתחנן לו״ – איני יודע מי נעשה שר למי
moves.summary: settles from a second verse that it was Jacob who prevailed over the angel
moves.about: bringing וישר אל מלאך as the verse whose ambiguity is then settled

moves.cueHe: ״בכה ויתחנן לו״ – איני יודע מי בכה למי
moves.summary: settles by the same method that it was the angel who wept to Jacob
moves.about: who wept to whom — ויאמר שלחני settles that the angel wept to Jacob

moves.cueHe: ״כי שרית עם אלהים ועם אנשים״, אמר רבה
moves.summary: reads the blessing as hinting at two princes from Jacob and at exile
moves.about: the angel hinted to Jacob that two princes would come from him — the Exilarch and the Nasi — and hinted at exile

moves.cueHe: ״ובגפן שלשה שריגים״, אמר רב חייא בר אבא אמר רב
moves.summary: opens the expositions of the butler's vine: the three branches are Israel's three princes each generation
moves.about: the three branches are the three proud princes of Israel in every generation, split between Babylonia and Eretz Yisrael

moves.cueHe: יהיבו רבנן עינייהו ברבנא עוקבא
moves.summary: the Sages present looked to Rabbana Ukva and Rabbana Nehemya as the two in Babylonia
moves.about: that the Sages present turned their eyes toward Rabbana Ukva and Rabbana Nehemya, the sons of Rav's daughter, as the princes in Babylonia

moves.summary: reads the branches instead as the angelic princes of the nations who defend Israel
moves.about: the three branches are the three angelic princes of the nations who plead for Israel in every generation

moves.cueHe: תניא, רבי אליעזר אומר: ״גפן״ – זה העולם
moves.summary: the vine is the world, the branches the patriarchs, the clusters the tribes
moves.about: the vine is the world, the three branches are the patriarchs, the blossoms the matriarchs, the clusters the tribes

moves.summary: defeats the reading: a dream shows only what is to come, and the patriarchs already were
moves.about: whether a man is shown in a dream what has already been, since the patriarchs and tribes preceded the butler's dream

moves.cueHe: אלא ״גפן״ – זה תורה
moves.summary: puts a forward-looking reading in its place: Torah, Moses Aaron and Miriam, the Sanhedrin, the righteous
moves.about: the vine is the Torah, the branches Moses, Aaron and Miriam, the blossoms the Sanhedrin, the clusters the righteous of each generation

moves.about: which reading of the butler's vine is required — Rabban Gamliel holds that only HaModa'i's, which refers every phrase to one place, will do

moves.cueHe: רבי אלעזר המודעי אומר: ״גפן״ – זה ירושלים
moves.summary: refers every phrase to Jerusalem: Temple, king, High Priest, young priests, libations
moves.about: the vine is Jerusalem, the branches the Temple, king and High Priest, the blossoms the young priests, the clusters the libations

moves.cueHe: רבי יהושע בן לוי מוקים לה במתנות
moves.summary: refers the verse to the gifts: Torah, the well, the cloud and the manna, first fruits, libations
moves.about: the vine is the Torah and the branches the well, the pillar of cloud and the manna — the gifts given to Israel

moves.cueHe: רבי ירמיה בר אבא אמר: ״גפן״ – אלו ישראל
moves.summary: refers the verse to Israel: the festivals, and the time to be fruitful and multiply
moves.about: the vine is the Jewish people, the branches the three pilgrimage festivals, and the budding their multiplying and redemption

moves.cueHe: ״עלתה נצה״ – הגיע זמן של ישראל ליגאל
moves.summary: continues: the blossoming is the time of redemption, the ripening Egypt's cup of fury
moves.about: bringing ויז נצחם for the time of Israel's redemption

moves.cueHe: והיינו דאמר רבא: שלשה כוסות האמורות במצרים למה
moves.summary: identifies this with Rava's three cups Egypt drinks — Moses, Pharaoh Nekho, and the end of days
moves.about: the three cups of Pharaoh's butler's dream are the three cups of misfortune Egypt drinks — in Moses' day, in Pharaoh Nekho's day, and in the future

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רבי אבא לרבי ירמיה בר אבא
moves.summary: tells Rabbi Yirmeya that Rav expounded these verses exactly as he does
moves.about: how Rav expounded these aggadic verses — Rabbi Abba reports that Rav read them as Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba does

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי שמעון בן לקיש: אומה זו כגפן נמשלה
moves.summary: extends the vine-as-Israel reading part by part: householders, scholars, ignoramuses, empty ones
moves.about: whether the vine of scripture signifies the Jewish people

moves.cueHe: והיינו דשלחו מתם: ליבעי רחמים איתכליא על עליא
moves.summary: the message from Eretz Yisrael: let the clusters pray for the leaves that sustain them
moves.about: citing the message sent from Eretz Yisrael that the clusters should pray for the leaves

moves.cueHe: ״ואכרה לי בחמשה עשר כסף״, אמר רבי יוחנן משום רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק
moves.summary: opens a new run on the leaders and righteous: kira in the verse means purchase
moves.about: Rabbi Yohanan reports Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak's exposition of ואכרה לי בחמשה עשר כסף

moves.cueHe: ״בחמשה עשר״ – זה חמשה עשר בניסן
moves.summary: the fifteen is the fifteenth of Nisan and the silver the righteous
moves.about: the fifteen is the fifteenth of Nisan, the silver the righteous, and the measures of barley the forty-five righteous who sustain the world

moves.cueHe: ״חומר שעורים ולתך שעורים״ – אלו ארבעים וחמשה צדיקים
moves.summary: the measures of barley are the forty-five righteous who sustain the world
moves.about: how the forty-five righteous are distributed — the thirty pieces of silver cast into the house of the Lord fix thirty in Eretz Yisrael and fifteen in Babylonia

moves.cueHe: כשהוא אומר: ״ואקחה שלשים הכסף״
moves.summary: settles their distribution from a second verse: thirty in Eretz Yisrael, fifteen in Babylonia

moves.cueHe: אמר אביי: ורובייהו משתכחי בבי כנישתא דתותי אפתא
moves.summary: adds that most of the fifteen are found in the synagogue under the upper room
moves.about: bringing וישקלו את שכרי שלשים כסף alongside the count of the righteous

moves.cueHe: רבי יהודה אומר: אלו שלשים צדיקי אומות העולם
moves.summary: reads the thirty instead as the righteous of the nations, in whose merit the nations endure
moves.about: the thirty are the thirty righteous of the nations of the world, in whose merit the nations endure

moves.cueHe: עולא אמר: אלו שלשים מצות שקבלו עליהם בני נח
moves.summary: reads the thirty as mitzvot the Noahides accepted, of which they keep only three
moves.about: the thirty are the thirty mitzvot the descendants of Noah accepted, of which they keep only three

moves.cueHe: שאין כותבין כתובה לזכרים
moves.summary: names the three they keep: no marriage contract for males, no selling human flesh, honouring the Torah
